title: Building a System
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/title: The Parts of a Trading System
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/0/bod: A **trading system** is a set of clear rules that tells you **what** to trade, **when** to enter, **where** to exit and **how much** to risk. A simple test: if two people run the same system, they should take **the same trades**.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/1/bod: Every complete system has these five parts. If one is missing, you'll be forced to **improvise** mid-trade, which is exactly where emotions sneak in.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/1/exa: The event that starts the entry
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/2/pai: The exact event that starts the entry
Where you exit when the idea was wrong
How much you risk on each trade
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/3/pro: Which one is NOT part of a trading system?
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/3/opt: A gut feeling about market direction
A clear rule for where the stop loss goes
A fixed percentage risked per trade
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/3/exp: A gut feeling can't be repeated or measured. A system is built from rules that play out the same way every time.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/4/sta: A system with entry rules but no exit rules is a complete system.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/4/exp: Half of every trade's result depends on the exit. Without stop loss and take profit rules, fear and greed decide when you get out.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/5/bod: Example: “On EUR/USD 1-hour, when price is above the **SMA 20** and a **bullish engulfing** forms near the average, buy. Stop loss below that candle's low, take profit at **2R**, risk **1%** of the account.” Every part is defined.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/5/tip: R is the amount you risk on one trade. 2R means a profit target twice your stop loss distance.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/6/pro: Using this system (price above SMA 20 + bullish engulfing near the average = buy), what signal does the last candle give?
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/6/exp: The average is pointing up, price closed above it, and the last candle fully engulfed the previous red candle's body. Both conditions are met, so by the rules, it's a buy.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/7/pro: Put the system's parts in the order you use them in a trade.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/7/ite: Set the stop loss and size
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/7/exp: First you know where to look for opportunities, then the setup forms and the trigger fires the entry. Stop loss and size are settled before you place the order.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/8/sen: If two people run the same system, they should take the ___ trades, because its rules are ___.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l1/steps/8/exp: A real system leaves no room for personal interpretation. That repeatability is what lets you test and improve it.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/0/bod: A good rule is **objective**: anyone who reads it makes the same call. “The trend is strong” is vague, but “price closed above the SMA 50 and the SMA 50 is higher than 10 candles ago” is **measurable**.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/1/bod: Write your rule as **“if … then …”**. If you couldn't teach it to a computer program, it's not precise yet. Swap **adjectives** for **numbers**: replace “big”, “strong” and “good” with specific values.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/2/opt: Buy when a 1-hour candle closes above resistance
Buy when the market feels good
Buy when price gets really cheap
Sell when you sense the trend is changing
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/2/exp: Everyone sees a candle close above a specific level the same way. “Feels good” and “really cheap” mean something different to each person.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/3/pro: Rule: “Buy when a candle closes above the 2420 line.” Tap the candle that triggers this rule.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/3/exp: Before this, wicks crossed 2420 several times but the candles closed below it. By the rule, those aren't signals. This is the first candle that closed above 2420.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/4/sta: “Buy when the trend is strong” is a measurable rule.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/4/exp: How strong is “strong”? Two people will read it two ways. It needs a number, like “ADX above 25” or “price above the SMA 50”.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/6/sen: Instead of adjectives like “strong” or “high”, a good rule uses ___ so it's ___.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/6/exp: Only a rule defined with numbers can be counted and tested on past data.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/7/pro: Why do you need measurable rules for a backtest?
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/7/opt: Without them, you can't count past results precisely and repeatably
They make sure no trade ever loses
The market always follows numeric rules
lessons/trading-system-u1-l2/steps/7/exp: With a vague rule, you get a different result every time you look back (usually in your own favor). A precise rule gives you real stats, not a guaranteed profit.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/0/bod: A **trading plan** is a written document that puts your trading system together with your **risk rules**, **trading hours** and **review routine**. The system says “how do I trade”; the plan says “how do I stay a trader”.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/1/bod: These rules prevent disaster days. When you hit your **daily loss limit**, you're done for the day, even if the best setup in the world is right in front of you.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/2/pro: Your account is $10,000, your daily loss limit is 3% and you risk 1% per trade. How many full losses in a row until you hit the daily limit?
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/2/exp: 3% of 10,000 = $300 and 1% = $100, so after 3 full losses, your trading day is over.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/3/pro: Put what you do before and after a trade in order.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/3/ite: Check the setup conditions against your plan
Decide where the stop loss and take profit go
Calculate size from your risk amount
Log the trade in your journal
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/3/exp: Size depends on the stop loss distance, so the stop loss spot comes first. The journal gets filled in after the trade is placed, so you can review it later.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/4/sta: You should change your trading plan after every losing trade.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/4/exp: Losses, even several in a row, are part of every system. Change your plan after reviewing enough trades, not out of emotion after one loss.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/5/pro: You've had 3 losses in a row today and hit your 3% daily loss limit. Now you see a perfect setup. What does your plan say to do?
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/5/opt: No more trades today; I'll pick it up tomorrow
Go in with double size to win it back
Take just this one with small size
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/5/exp: The daily loss limit exists for exactly this moment, when your mind is primed for revenge trading after a few losses. Good setups will still be there tomorrow.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/6/sen: When you hit your daily loss ___, you ___ trading for the day.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/6/exp: A daily loss limit is a brake you set in advance, so one bad day doesn't turn into a bad week.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/7/bod: Your plan changes with **data**, not emotion. Every week or month, go through your journal: did you trade by the plan? Which rules did you break? Fix your **execution** of the plan first, then think about changing the system itself.
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/8/pro: In your monthly review, you see that 6 of your 20 trades broke your plan's rules, and most of the losses came from those. What's the sensible first step?
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/8/opt: Execute the plan precisely before changing anything in the system
Remove the stop loss from the plan
lessons/trading-system-u1-l3/steps/8/exp: Until you execute the plan precisely, you can't tell whether the problem is the system or your execution. This month's data says the main problem is execution.
